When dinosaurs come knocking. Hot off the box office success of “The Odyssey,” Anne Hathaway stars alongside Obi-Wan Kenobi actor Ewan McGregor in a thrilling prehistoric dinosaur flick. Dinosaur films seem to be a rarity, save for the usual “Jurassic Park” box office releases. Perhaps it’s because most viewers might assume it's all the same. Thankfully, “The End of Oak Street” offers something different that makes it stand out from the already established franchise. In “The End of Oak Street,” we follow the Platt family. Anne and Ewan take on the roles of Denise and Greg, a couple on the brink of divorce, as they try to keep things together for their two kids. One night, an unexplained phenomenon sends their entire block to a mysterious location millions of years in the past. Prehistoric creatures prey on their neighbors one by one, leaving the family no other choice but to survive as long as they can. What makes this film truly enjoyable is its thrilling action. Dinosaurs range from downright adorable to absolute apex predators. It's also admirable that the film features lesser-known species to keep things fresh. Sometimes the creatures just roam around in the background, making the film’s environment feel more lived in by these prehistoric critters. When there is a threat that lingers, you are left on the edge of your seat, begging for characters to either run or turn around. It makes for a frustratingly good time. Now, our only personal gripe with the film is its somewhat rushed end. It leaves many questions unanswered and tries to write it off as an unexplainable phenomenon. Vague spoiler alert: It also ends with a time paradox. This will likely make or break the entire experience for viewers, but personally, it was enough to lead to an exciting tangent of trying to dive and debate with other viewers about the time-travel aspect of the film. Catch it in theaters, form an opinion, and start debating about the timeline once you’ve seen the ending. Manila Bulletin Lifestyle was invited to an advanced screening of “The End of Oak Street” held at Uptown Mall’s Ultra Cinema. It is now showing in cinemas nationwide.

Chinese EV makers targeting Japanese market. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Chinese automakers are banking on the Japanese electric vehicle market as they struggle with slowing growth in their home market and high tariffs in the United States and Europe. BYD Co., a Chinese electric vehicle giant, released the Racco, a mini vehicle developed exclusively for the Japanese market, on July 28. BYD Vice President Liu Xueliang said at a launch event in Tokyo that the company will work to win a Japanese market share in the long run. The automaker hired a former engineer at Japanese automaker Nissan Motor Co. who led the development of its Sakura electric mini vehicle to develop the Racco. The BYD electric mini vehicle features automatic sliding doors popular among families with children and includes equipment such as an umbrella stand and a cup holder with heat insulation. BYD sold about 4.6 million units globally last year, with growth primarily in Southeast Asia and Europe. It overtook U.S. automaker Tesla Inc. as the world's largest electric vehicle manufacturer. In its home market, however, new car sales have slowed as the Chinese government reduced incentives for electric vehicle purchases. Tariffs pose a significant challenge for Chinese automakers. The United States imposes 100 pct tariffs on Chinese-made EVs, and the European Union has raised tariffs on them. In Japan where there are no such tariffs, BYD is cooperating with local importers to build a nationwide sales network. Chery Automobile Co., a Chinese automaker, has announced plans to jointly develop an electric mini vehicle with Autobacs Seven Co., a Japanese auto parts maker, for sale in Japan as early as next year. Zeekr, a luxury Chinese electric vehicle brand, plans to release a high-priced electric minivan in Japan. "Although the penetration rate of EVs is low compared with the United States and Europe, there are fewer restrictions and it is easier to enter," Hiroyuki Shimizu of international consulting firm AlixPartners said of the Japanese market. It is a "low-risk, low-return market," he said. In contrast, Go Meiken of TNC Research & Consulting said, "It's difficult to imagine that Japanese consumers who want high quality are eager to buy Chinese vehicles." He added, "It's also a challenge whether they can expand sales and maintenance networks" to promote EVs in rural areas.

2nd District of Valenzuela receives 250 hygiene kits from PCSO. Representing the PCSO, Executive Assistant VI Atty. Maria Katrina Nicole Contacto-Ventanilla led the ceremonial turnover on July 23, 2026, at the agency’s Executive Office, 4th Floor, Sun Plaza Building in Mandaluyong City. The hygiene kits were received by Chief of Staff Sherluck Estrella, representing the 2nd District of Valenzuela. Japan moving fast to tighten regulations on foreigners. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- The administration of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is moving fast to tighten regulations on foreign residents in the country, as it seeks to ease concerns among some Japanese people about a sharp increase in foreigners. The government last month announced a plan to significantly increase fees for residence status applications. Earlier this month, it unveiled a plan to tighten conditions for obtaining permanent residence. Under the immigration control and refugee recognition law, obtaining permanent residence requires good behavior, having sufficient assets and skills to support independent living and it being in the national interest. The Immigration Services Agency earlier this month announced a plan to revise guidelines for permanent residence, adding a requirement that applicants have annual income levels exceeding the average in Japan and projected pension benefits equivalent to those after 30 years of participation in the "kosei nenkin" public pension program for employees. The revised guidelines also require applicants to make active and tangible contributions to Japan. The agency plans to begin applying these changes in stages starting in October. The revision comes amid concerns about the failure by some foreign residents to pay taxes and social insurance premiums. "We will ensure that granting permanent residence will not place a burden on the public," Justice Minister Hiroshi Hiraguchi said of the revised guidelines at a press conference on Aug. 4. Some experts expressed worries about the revised guidelines. "Imposing strict requirements equivalent to laws (under guidelines) infringes on the authority of parliament," said Shoichi Ibusuki, a lawyer familiar with foreign resident issues. The Takaichi administration also tightened conditions for obtaining Japanese nationality, extending necessary residence terms from five years or more to 10 years or more in principle. The country will raise permanent residence fees by 20-fold to 200,000 yen in October. An advisory panel to the government has started discussing the possibility of controlling the ratio of foreign residents to the country's total population. The number of foreign residents in Japan hit a record high of 4,125,395 as of the end of 2025. "A rapid increase in foreign residents could cause social anxiety and stir up xenophobic sentiment," a former cabinet minister in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party said. "Strict conditions are necessary to accept foreigners." But an increase in foreigners in Japan is partly because of a decline in the working-age population in the country. Japan faces competition with countries such as South Korea in obtaining foreign talent. "Japan will become less attractive if no measures are taken," a lawmaker in the main opposition Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan said. "Economic activity would shrink and communities could not be sustained if foreigners do not come to live in Japan."

Exploring the local favorites of Taiwan. When visiting Taiwan, it’s almost a given that Taipei has most of what you’re looking for. Of course, there’s the Taipei 101 building, which towers above everything else and is visible from miles away. On an equally grand scale is the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, where Taiwan’s rich history can be explored. Then there are countless night markets to wander through and empty your wallets at, with parlor games, souvenirs, thrift finds, and Michelin-recommended food stalls to enjoy. There are, however, even more hidden-gem destinations that are sure to leave lasting memories if you seek them out. One such stop is the Danjiang Bridge. While it might seem unusual to consider a busy highway a tourist attraction, you’d be surprised by how many locals frequent the area, especially after sunset on weekends. That’s largely because the bridge features a dedicated lane for cyclists and pedestrians to enjoy at their own pace. Take a short walk farther, and you’ll find a cozy spot shaded by trees that offers a perfect view of the bridge and the river below. Several food stalls also begin opening in the late afternoon. Once you’ve taken in the view, get ready for another short walk to Tamsui Old Street. It’s about a 15-minute walk away, and along the way you’ll come across charming cafés and museums worth visiting. You can also stop by Fuyou Temple to take a breather before continuing your journey. Take your time exploring. Once you arrive, you’re sure to find something that piques your interest. During our visit, one particular shop stood out because of its unique façade. At its entrance, a shark loomed over passersby. Inside, the space felt like a cross between the Mystery Shack and a Ripley’s Believe It or Not! museum, with all kinds of oddities on display. There were live insects and arachnids, as well as taxidermied specimens that visitors could view for free. If you’re willing to spend a little more, there’s also a museum inside that you can explore. For a truly off-the-beaten-path experience, make your way to the Maokong Gondola for a cable car ride offering one of the best views of the city. Although it’s still within Taipei, the abundance of trees and lush greenery makes it feel like an entirely different world. Urban life and nature blend seamlessly in the Maokong area. There’s a zoo and a temple to visit, but the main attraction lies at the final gondola stop. Once you arrive, make your way to the Mei Jia Tea Garden. It’s quite a walk to get there, but the view is well worth the effort. Take your time to relax, soak in the scenery, and sip freshly brewed tea. The tea house also features a small museum that showcases its rich history. If these sites entice you to know more about the beauty of Taiwan, consider dropping by the Taiwan 100 Ways event set to take place at One Ayala, Makati, from Aug. 22 to 23.

Quake-hit Kumamoto's tourism sector suffers ¥6 billion blow. KUMAMOTO (Jiji Press) -- Amid the summer holiday season, the tourism industry in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, is suffering a 6-billion-yen blow from the recent massive earthquake. According to the prefectural government, the July 28 earthquake, which measured the maximum seismic intensity level of 7 on the Japanese scale, caused about 4.04 billion yen in damage to hotel buildings and equipment. Additionally, about 146,000 people canceled hotel bookings by Aug. 6, resulting in losses of about 2.06 billion yen. About 60 pct of the cancellations were made in the Aso and Amakusa areas, despite relatively little damage from the quake there. Warning against ungrounded information, Kumamoto Governor Takashi Kimura said, "There are unaffected areas even in the prefecture." After the quake, a "ryokan" Japanese-style inn in the city of Kamiamakusa faced a flurry of cancellations of bookings until autumn. It had already been struggling with damage from last August's flooding, as well as soaring costs, while still recovering from the COVID-19 crisis. "There's no light at the end of the tunnel," said the inn's landlady, Kayomi Nakashima, 58. "We've tried to stay positive, but after seeing disasters continue like this, we're (at a loss)." Aso Farm Land, a leisure facility in the village of Minamiaso, has seen the number of visitors drop to around half of the average-year level. Bookings for overnight stays at the facility from about 4,800 people were canceled by Monday, resulting in a revenue loss of about 100 million yen. "August is usually a busy period for us, but the number of bookings continues to decrease," said Masakazu Higashi, a 56-year-old manager of the facility. The Aso Volcano Museum, located in a tourist area in the city of Aso, was also hit by a visitor number slump to a third of usual levels in the week after the quake, with bookings from about 400 people, mainly those on school trips and other group tours, canceled. Two weeks after the quake, visitors are beginning to return to the museum, but many are still worried about aftershocks. The museum continues to inform the public on social media that it is open as usual. "We hope things go back to normal soon," said Katsunori Toyomura, a 40-year-old curator at the museum. A ryokan in the city of Kumamoto has received many booking cancellations for the rest of this year, including a holiday period in September, and has also experienced a fall in demand for drinking parties. The inn sustained damage from the quake, including to tiles in the women's bath, but it has been able to operate and has accepted evacuees. According to its landlady, Ai Hirayama, 51, the inn had offered its "onsen" hot spring facility to people working on restoration work after the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes. "We hope people take a break at our facility when they're tired," said Hirayama. "We take great pride in being a ryokan offering hot water, a gift from nature."

Japan protests Putin's visit to disputed island. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday condemned Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to one of the four northwestern Pacific islands claimed by Tokyo but controlled by Moscow. Putin's visit to Etorofu, one of the islands Japan calls the Northern Territories, is "incompatible with Japan's consistent position and is absolutely unacceptable," Takaichi told reporters at her official residence. She said Tokyo "strongly protests" the trip, adding, "The Northern Territories are an inherent part of our country's territory both historically and under international law." The prime minister discussed possible responses with officials including Keiichi Ichikawa, secretary-general of the National Security Secretariat, and Vice Foreign Minister Takehiro Funakoshi. Later in the day, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi summoned Russian Ambassador to Japan Nikolay Nozdrev to the Foreign Ministry and lodged a protest. Takaichi told reporters that she learned of Putin's visit to Etorofu on Thursday afternoon. The visit came as a surprise, a Japanese government source said. Russia's state-run news agency Tass reported that the president visited the island Thursday. "This visit has further hardened Japanese public sentiment against Russia and made it difficult to improve bilateral relations in the medium to long term," she said. "We want the Russian side to take the gravity of this matter seriously." The Russian-controlled islands were seized by the former Soviet Union from Japan at the end of World War II and have long been claimed by Japan. The territorial row has prevented Tokyo and Moscow from concluding a peace treaty to formally end their wartime hostilities. The Takaichi administration has continued to impose sanctions against Russia following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, which started in February 2022, in step with other Group of Seven major democracies. It has been increasing vigilance over Russian military exercises in the waters around the Northern Territories and deeper military cooperation between Russia and China. At the same time, Tokyo has pursued diplomacy with Moscow amid energy security concerns stemming from the turmoil over Iran, as well as concerns about the potential impact of the Middle East situation on the Northern Territories issue. As part of such efforts, senior officials from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry visited Russia in May. Motegi chatted with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov at a foreign ministers meeting linked to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in the Philippines last month. Former residents of Etorofu island expressed outrage over Putin's visit. Yuzo Matsumoto, 85, who was born on the island and lived there until the age of 4, said he feels as though his "hometown has been trampled on." Matsumoto, who heads a group of former residents of the Northern Territories, said he is "extremely frustrated and disappointed." According to the group, the number of former residents of the Northern Territories stood at about 4,700 as of June, with their average age topping 90. "It is deeply upsetting to former residents who were forced out," said Takako Yamashita, 62, who engages in advocacy work regarding the disputed islands with her mother, who is from Etorofu. "It's frustrating to be unable to do anything."

Lynk & Co to become Geely Motor Philippines subsidiary. Lynk & Co cars will now be distributed by Geely Motor Philippines (GMP) and will function as its subsidiary. Formerly distributed by United Asia Automotive Group Inc. (UAAGI), the brand will be officially integrated into the Geely group in the Philippines, aligning with its global operations. This realignment is part of the "One Geely" strategy to escalate its long-term investment in the Philippine market. Under Geely’s established local operational foundation and resource capabilities in the Philippines, Lynk & Co can enhance its market responsiveness, accelerate product introduction and market expansion, and continuously address the evolving demands of local consumers for premium mobility. Lynk & Co also plans to accelerate the development of its sales and service network, establishing a more solid localized foundation for the brand's long-term growth. "We sincerely appreciate United Asia Automotive Group Inc. (UAAGI) for their continuous support and contributions to Lynk & Co's growth in the Philippines," said Mr. Ye Qin, General Manager of ASEAN RHD Business Unit, Geely Auto International Corporation. "Since Lynk & Co entered the Philippine market, UAAGI has actively driven the brand's local market development, laying a foundation for expanding our presence and serving local consumers.” “The Philippines remains a crucial market for Lynk & Co’s long-term development. Moving forward, we will continue to increase our investment in the Philippine market, enrich our product lineup, optimize our sales and service infrastructure, and enhance user experience, delivering better mobility experiences tailored to local consumer needs." A new flagship model Despite the move, Lynk & Co has no plans of slowing down. In the fourth quarter of 2026, Lynk & Co will start its brand refreshment in the Philippines and progressively introduce a new generation of premium products under the GMP operating framework. Among these is the Lynk & Co 900, a high-tech, full-size SUV targeted at the premium PHEV segment. As Lynk & Co’s flagship SUV, the Lynk & Co 900 centers around exceptional space, comfort, safety, delivering a refined experience that seamlessly balances comfort and smart capabilities for family premium travel. Driven by its flagship-grade capabilities, the Lynk & Co 900 is set to meet the diverse needs of Filipino consumers seeking high-quality family mobility, introducing a compelling new option to the local premium new energy market. The Lynk & Co 900 is scheduled to launch in the Philippines in the fourth quarter of 2026, with detailed product specifications and launch arrangements to be disclosed in due course.

First Lady leads rice aid distribution to senior citizens in Bacolod City. BACOLOD CITY - First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos led the distribution of the second tranche of rice aid to thousands of senior citizens in this highly-urbanized city on Friday, August 14. The first lady was joined by city officials led by Mayor Greg Gasataya, Bacolod Rep. and House Deputy Speaker Albee Benitez, and Nanay Partylist Rep. Florabel Yatco in the rice distribution to 2,000 beneficiaries at STI-West Negros University gymnasium here. Each beneficiary, who is not part of the social pension program, aged 65 and above, received 10 kilos of rice. In her message, the First Lady expressed her joy in being able to visit the city and lead the rice assistance on behalf of her husband, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. “Bilang isang ina, alam ko na mahalaga ang pagkain sa bawat mesa. Konting bagay lang po ito. But I hope, it could help you in the days to come,” she said. Gasataya thanked the President for providing the assistance directly to the beneficiaries. “For the first time, there’s a national government program that directly goes to the people,” he said. Gasataya said the national government is ready to assist and help the people especially in difficult times. In a media interview on the sideline of the event, Gasataya said the city targeted 35,000 beneficiaries, with the first distribution held last July. The remaining two tranches are set in October and November. The mayor said the announcement for the rice distribution dates will be posted by their respective barangays. “All are in place,” he added. For 80-year-old Leonora of Barangay Vista Alegre, she expressed her gratitude for the assistance that could help alleviate her family’s situation. The initiative forms part of the national government’s “Bawat Bayan Makikinabang” Program which aims to address the needs of Filipinos, especially the vulnerable communities.

Philippines, Chile mark 80 years of ties with push for trade, maritime cooperation. The Philippines and Chile are seeking to deepen bilateral relations as the two Pacific nations mark 80 years of diplomatic ties, with trade, investment, maritime cooperation, and tourism among the areas identified for closer collaboration. In statements issued on Friday, August 14, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro met with Chilean President José Antonio Kast Rist at the Palacio de La Moneda in Santiago, where she conveyed President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s greetings and renewed Manila’s commitment to strengthening relations with Chile. “Honored to meet with Chilean President José Antonio Kast and extend the warmest greetings of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.,” Lazaro said in a post on X. “I reiterated our commitment to deepening PH-Chile ties, now that we are close to finalizing our bilateral Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), during the milestone 80th anniversary of diplomatic relations,” she added. Lazaro and Kast discussed the potential of the CEPA to expand trade and investment between the two APEC economies. “The Pacific Ocean does not separate us, it links our destinies,” Lazaro said, underscoring the Philippines’ interest in expanding its partnership with Chile. She also invited Kast to visit the Philippines. The meeting came shortly after the conclusion of negotiations for the Philippines-Chile CEPA. The agreement, which was concluded in July, is aimed at strengthening trade and investment ties between the two countries. Philippines-Chile trade ties Lazaro’s official visit to Santiago also included a bilateral meeting with Chilean Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The two officials discussed economic cooperation, including trade and investment, as well as maritime and consular cooperation. They had previously met on the sidelines of the commemorative activity for the 50th anniversary of the ASEAN Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia in Manila in July 2026. In an X post, Lazaro said she and Pérez Mackenna had “productive talks” during her official visit to Santiago. “Commemorating 80 years of PH-CL diplomatic ties, we welcome the imminent signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, the Philippines’ first bilateral trade agreement in Latin America,” Lazaro said. Tourism, people-to-people exchanges Lazaro said she also signed a memorandum of understanding on tourism between the Philippines and Chile. “I also signed an agreement on tourism cooperation showing our ever-expanding partnership with Chile,” she added. Lazaro said the agreement could create greater opportunities for both countries and strengthen their economic links. The agreement is expected to facilitate closer cooperation between the two countries’ tourism authorities and promote greater people-to-people exchanges. The talks also covered regional and international issues of mutual interest. 80 years of Philippines-Chile diplomatic relations Lazaro said the official visit, which coincided with the 80th anniversary of Philippines-Chile diplomatic relations, “reaffirms our shared commitment to strengthening the friendship and cooperation between our two Pacific-facing nations.” She also hailed the recent conclusion of negotiations for the Philippines-Chile CEPA, which would “leave the gates wide open for immense trade and investment opportunities, making our two countries more interconnected and interdependent than ever before.” The Philippines and Chile established diplomatic relations on July 4, 1946, the day the Philippines gained independence. The two countries are marking the 80th anniversary of their diplomatic ties in 2026 through increased engagement in economic, maritime, tourism, and other areas of cooperation. As of the end of 2025, about 1,017 Filipinos made up the Filipino community in Chile. COA mulls fraud audit vs OVP, DepEd over ‘unusual’ recipients of confidential funds. The Commission on Audit (COA) is studying the possibility of launching a fraud audit against the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) over the “unusual” names of the recipients of confidential funds from the two agencies that were both then under Vice President Sara Duterte. COA auditor Xylene Mae del Campo disclosed this to the Senate Impeachment Court on Day 15 of the impeachment trial after Sen. Paolo “Bam” Aquino IV asked her if they have conducted a fraud audit on the use of the confidential funds by the OVP and DepEd. “It is still being studied with Chairperson (Gamaliel Cordoba),” del Campo told the impeachment court. “If a fraud audit were to be conducted, this would be the first time…The documents—the transactions involving the OVP and DepEd—consist of a voluminous amount of records containing sensitive information; if these were turned over to another office, that information could be exposed,” she said. According to Aquino, he and his lawyers have consulted former COA Commissioner Heidi Mendoza over the “strange” names of supposed recipients of the OVP and DepEd’s confidential funds which include “Mary Grace Piattos” who supposedly received P70,000, “Ralph Joseph Bacon” who is said to have been given P150,000 and “Matthew N Keso” who supposedly received P250,000. “There’s Piattos, Bacon, Heart, Keso, and so on. Didn’t you consider this a red flag?” Aquino asked. “Some of our lawyers consulted former Commissioner Heidi Mendoza, and she said that when there are unusual names, the COA can trigger an investigation due to fraud,” he pointed out. The COA auditor said they have not yet looked deeper into the seemingly fraudulent names used by recipients of the OVP and DepEd’s confidential funds since they were assuming regularity in their transactions. She pointed out that the Special Disbursing Officers (SDO) of both offices under Duterte declared under oath that the money was used for confidential operations. But Aquino went on to say that Republic Act No. 6085 prohibits the use of aliases and stressing that government auditing rules require that each acknowledgement receipt must strictly correspond to a real, verifiable individual.

Independent space warrior Count Binface seeks seat in UK Parliament. As ridiculous as it sounds, independent space warrior Count Binface just might have a shot at having a seat within the UK Parliament. All eyes in the UK are on Clacton right now as a tense battle between Count Binface and UK Reform Party candidate Nigel Farage. Nigel had previously won the Clacton seat but quit to trigger a by-election after facing scrutiny over an undeclared donation worth ₱414 million (£5M). In protest, the UK's most prominent parties, Labour and Conservative, opted not to participate in the election. This led the door open for just about anyone to face off against Nigel, hence Count Binface. Count Binface has long been a familiar face in UK politics, having faced off against three Prime Ministers in the past. Behind the bin is Jon Harvey, a British satirist who has worked in several comedy television programs. He first took on the mantle of Lord Buckethead to face off against former Prime Minister Theresa May in the 2017 general election before dropping the character due to copyright issues. Since then, Jon has taken on the persona of Count Binface to run in different elections in the UK. It's a fascinating glimpse into how the UK political system operates. For this by-election, the UK broke its record for the most candidates vying for the top spot, with a total of 34 candidates. Through polls, Nigel and Count Binface remain the top choices for the seat. People have clamored that it's a "bin-bin (win-win)" situation for Count Binface due to how it makes Nigel look either way. If Nigel wins, he wins against what many deem a nuisance candidate. If Count Binface wins, Nigel would have to live with the fact that he just lost to a man with a bin on his head. Even if Nigel wins, the investigation into his funds also continues. What's amusing about a candidate like Count Binface gaining such a position is that it shows the baffling nature of the UK's political system. For Count Binface, his being allowed to run shows how the centuries-old model of democracy is beautiful, since it shows that even the most high-profile candidates are above no one. In the UK, anyone is allowed to run provided they meet the rules and shell out ₱41,426 (£500). This amount is returned if they manage to receive up to five percent of the votes cast. With this ruling, many prominent joke candidates have popped up in the UK over the years, including the political party known as the Monster Raving Loony Party. In the Philippines, while a candidate similar to Count Binface could go viral, they are not likely to ever appear on the voting sheets. Voters from 2016 might recall when Allan Carreon gained momentary fame after claiming to be an intergalactic ambassador for the Philippines. Even if just about anyone can freely file their Certificate of Candidacy (COC) to run for any position, the Commission on Elections is tasked with weeding out anyone classified as nuisance candidates. According to the Omnibus Election Code, a nuisance candidate is classified as someone who either files a COC solely to mock or discredit the election process, a candidacy that causes confusion by having or mimicking the name of registered candidates, or those whose actions or circumstances demonstrate a lack of general intent to run for office. With the Clacton polls now officially closed, the vote count of Nigel Farage vs. Count Binface is underway. It's still unknown what would happen if Count Binface manages to win over Nigel. Would the UK Parliament permit him to join as his intergalactic identity? Only time will tell.

Chiba downpour leaves 4 dead, 1 in cardiac arrest. CHIBA, Aug. 14 (Jiji Press) -- Heavy rain in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, left four people dead and another in cardiopulmonary arrest before subsiding in the small hours of Friday, according to the prefectural disaster response headquarters. The Japan Meteorological Agency downgraded Level 5 emergency heavy rain and landslide warnings issued for many municipalities in Chiba to Level 4 warnings or lower under the five-level alert system at 5:15 a.m. Friday. The agency continued to urge the public to remain on high alert for landslides, swollen rivers, inundation of low-lying areas and flooding. In the eastern Kanto-Koshin region, unstable atmospheric conditions and the risk of heavy rain will continue through Saturday morning. According to the disaster response headquarters, the victims included one person in Ichikawa and two in Sakura. The remaining victim was found in Yachiyo. One person is unaccounted for in the city of Chiba, while another is in cardiopulmonary arrest in Kashiwa. As of 6 a.m. Friday, a total of 359 evacuation centers had been set up in the prefecture, with 7,359 people from 3,855 households taking shelter there, according to the headquarters. Many residents were unable to return home, with about 4,000 people temporarily staying near East Japan Railway Co.'s Soga Station in Chuo Ward in the city of Chiba. The Ground Self-Defense Force transported them to evacuation centers by bus and other means. About 7,000 people stranded at Narita International Airport in the city of Narita stayed overnight at the facility. In the prefecture, linear precipitation zones intermittently developed from Thursday evening, and the agency issued record-breaking short-term rainfall information 25 times in total. In Chuo Ward in the prefectural capital, rainfall reached 115.0 millimeters in an hour through 6:45 p.m. Thursday and 348.0 millimeters in the 12 hours through 1:40 a.m. Friday, both marking records for the area. The heavy rain was caused by warm, moist air flowing from the southeast around a high-pressure system near the Chishima island chain off Hokkaido, northernmost Japan, colliding with northerly winds. Cold air aloft also contributed to the formation of cumulonimbus clouds in the area. The maximum 24-hour rainfall through 6 a.m. Saturday is forecast at 150 millimeters in the southern Kanto region, 120 millimeters in the northern Kanto region and 80 millimeters in the Koshin region.

DILG places Luisiana, Laguna mayor under 90-day preventive suspension. LUISIANA, Laguna- The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has served a 90-day preventive suspension order on Luisiana Mayor Jomapher Uy Alvarez in connection with the case filed against him for violating Section 3(f) of Republic Act 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Following a Regional Trial Court's order, Alvarez is temporarily unable to perform his duties as mayor while the hearing on the case is ongoing. Concurrently, the court denied the Motion to Quash filed by Alvarez's camp. The court clarified that the preventive suspension is merely part of the standard judicial process and does not imply that Alvarez has been finally convicted. Vice Mayor Jonieces Acaylar was sworn in as acting municipal mayor on Wednesday, August 12, by presiding judge Shari-Christine SJ Almario. According to Acaylar, the case stemmed from the alleged non-payment of terminal leave benefits to former Luisiana Mayor Nestor Rondilla, who filed the complaint against Alvarez. The newly installed acting mayor assured the public that all programs and public services in the town of Luisiana would continue while the three-month suspension order against Alvarez remains in effect.

Marcos vows accountability for anomalous infrastructure projects amid flood risks. President Marcos has vowed to hold accountable all individuals responsible for the anomalous implementation of government infrastructure projects, stressing that the government must ensure these projects deliver the protection and services Filipinos need. Speaking at the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (FOCAP) Presidential Luncheon in Manila on Friday, Aug. 14, Marcos said the commitment he made during his State of the Nation Address (SONA) last month remains a priority as the country faces heightened risks from flooding during the rainy season. “We will hold accountable all individuals responsible for the anomalous implementation of government infrastructure projects,” he said. The President said the accountability drive must go hand in hand with ensuring that infrastructure projects actually deliver the services required by communities. Flood mitigation President Marcos said the need to strengthen flood mitigation and disaster preparedness has become more urgent as communities across the country face increased risks from flooding and other hazards associated with the rainy season. “We are strengthening flood mitigation and disaster preparedness, and accelerating the implementation of critical interventions,” he said. Marcos stressed that public funds used for infrastructure projects must result in tangible protection for communities. “Every peso invested in these projects must translate into real protection for our people and our communities,” he said. Government credibility, public trust Meanwhile, Marcos said effective governance should not be measured only by the projects the government builds, but also by the trust it earns from the public. He said credibility is a shared responsibility between government and the media, particularly as false, fabricated, AI-generated, and deliberately manipulated information can spread rapidly across digital platforms. “In that regard, you, in your role as journalists, and I, as a public servant, have something important in common: our credibility,” Marcos said, adding that credibility is the foundation of their work and the bedrock of public trust. Marcos said a responsible and independent media remains essential in informing the public, scrutinizing those in power, and helping ensure that facts prevail over speculation and fake news.

Philip Morris Philippines earns Great Place To Work certification. Philip Morris Philippines, composed of PMFTC Inc. and PMI Business Solutions (Philippines) Inc. (PMIBS), has bagged the Great Place To Work certification, reaffirming its commitment to building a workplace culture anchored on trust, inclusion, collaboration, and continuous growth. Joseph Gruber, Head of People & Culture at PMFTC, said the recognition reflects the company’s belief that business transformation begins with its people. “Earning this certification for the first time is especially meaningful because it comes directly from the voices of our employees. Their trust and commitment make PMFTC and PMIBS truly great places to work, where everyone feels empowered to grow and inspired to contribute to our shared purpose of delivering a smoke-free future. When our people succeed and feel valued, our business transformation becomes stronger and more sustainable,” he said. It is the sole official recognition earned by the real-time feedback of employees regarding their company culture. “Great Place To Work Certification is a highly coveted achievement that requires consistent and intentional dedication to the overall employee experience,” says Sarah Lewis-Kulin, Vice President of Global Recognition at Great Place To Work. “By successfully earning this recognition, it is evident that Philip Morris Philippines (PMFTC/PMIBS) stands out as one of the top companies to work for, providing a great workplace environment for its employees,” she added. The Philippine certification builds on a growing number of Great Place To Work recognitions received by Philip Morris International (PMI) affiliates around the world. For 2025-2026, six PMI affiliates have earned Great Place To Work certifications across Latin America, Asia, and Europe, reflecting the company’s broader focus on creating positive employee experiences across its global operations. The latest milestone brings Philip Morris Philippines alongside other PMI affiliates around the world that have received Great Place To Work recognition, reinforcing the company’s commitment to investing in its people as it continues its aim to actively deliver a smoke-free future.

Jollibee wins 11 Marketing Excellence Awards, earns YouTube Works recognition. Jollibee brought home 11 awards at the 2026 Marketing Excellence Awards, including Gold for Marketing Team of the Year, adding to the brand's recent recognition at the YouTube Works Awards Philippines. The Philippines' number one fast food chain was recognized across categories covering digital commerce, customer engagement, content marketing, influencer marketing, advertising, and mobile marketing, further highlighting the breadth of its marketing work across platforms and consumer touchpoints. “These awards belong to every member of our marketing team and our agency partners, whose passion and creativity bring the joy of Jollibee to life. We are deeply honored by this recognition, especially being named Marketing Team of the Year. It inspires us to keep raising the bar and creating meaningful work that resonates with Filipinos and makes a real difference in their lives,” said Dorothy Ching, vice president for marketing of Jollibee Philippines. The Jollibee App led the company's digital wins, earning Gold for Excellence in Omnichannel Marketing, Silver for Excellence in e-Commerce Marketing and Launch Marketing, and Bronze for Excellence in Performance Marketing. National Day of Joy and Jollibee Joy Run also earned Gold for Excellence in Customer Engagement and Excellence in Mobile Marketing, respectively. Jolly Takam Shots received Silver for Excellence in Content Marketing, while JolliCreators earned Silver for Excellence in Influencer/KOLs Marketing. GameJoy Combos won Bronze for Excellence in Advertising, while Ching was also recognized with Bronze for Marketing Leader of the Year. Jollibee also recently received recognition at the YouTube Works Awards Philippines for its 2025 Christmas campaign, Buo ang Saya ng Pasko. The campaign won the Multiformat Storytelling category and was named 2nd runner-up for Best of Philippines.
