Fisherman wanted for carnapping, robbery nabbed in Taguig. Personnel of the Taguig Police Warrant and Subpoena Section arrested a 22-year-old fisherman facing carnapping and robbery cases in Taguig on Aug. 12. The suspect, identified as alias John Michael, a resident of Barangay Palingon Tipas, was classified by the Taguig police as a most wanted person. Police officers served a warrant of arrest at his residence on Magsalin Street in the barangay. The warrant, with no bail recommended, was issued on Aug. 11 by Presiding Judge Romeo Carmelito Caneja Conge of the Binangonan, Rizal Regional Trial Court Branch 67 for two cases of carnapping (Section 3 of Republic Act 10883) and robbery (Article 294 of the Revised Penal Code). The suspect was brought to the Taguig City Health Office for medical examination before being turned over to the Warrant and Subpoena Section office. Southern Police District director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco lauded the Taguig police for their efforts to track down wanted persons.

Man, 68, arrested in Taguig for lascivious acts vs niece. Authorities arrested a 68-year-old man for allegedly committing acts of lasciviousness against his 13-year-old niece in Barangay Rizal, Taguig, on Aug. 13. According to Taguig police, at about 11:40 a.m., the victim was preparing to go to school inside their residence when she was confronted by the suspect, identified as alias “RRCP.” Fearing for her safety, the victim immediately left the house and reported the incident to a friend and her friend’s mother, who promptly sought assistance from barangay authorities. Barangay Security Force (BSF) officers apprehended the suspect and turned him over to personnel of Taguig Police Sub-Station 10. The suspect was brought to the police station for documentation and will face criminal charges for violation of Article 336 (acts of lasciviousness) of the Revised Penal Code. Southern Police District director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco commended the Taguig police and barangay officials for their swift action.

Weeklong rains push Angat Dam to minimum operating level. Angat Dam in Bulacan has recovered to its 180-meter minimum operating level as rains from the southwest monsoon or “habagat” continue to boost water levels, based on the monitoring of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) on Friday, Aug. 14. As of 8 a.m. Friday, the dam’s water level rose to 180.10 meters, up 1.31 meters from 178.79 meters recorded the previous day. The 180-meter mark is Angat Dam’s minimum operating level, an important threshold used in managing the reservoir’s water supply. When the water level falls below this point, the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) may reduce water allocations as available supply becomes more limited, while prioritizing domestic water needs. Meanwhile, Angat’s 160-meter mark is considered its critical level, indicating a more serious shortage and the need for tighter water management. The dam’s return to the minimum operating level marks a significant improvement after its water level plunged to a record-low 150.6 meters on July 25, when it was also below the critical level. Despite the recovery, Angat Dam remains nearly 30 meters below its 210-meter normal high water level during the rainy season. Continued gains are needed to build up the reservoir’s water reserves ahead of the next dry season. Meanwhile, Ambuklao and Binga dams in Benguet continued to release water on Friday. Ambuklao Dam’s water level was at 751.61 meters, just 0.19 meter below its normal high water level, while Binga Dam was at 574.89 meters, or 0.08 meter below its normal high water level. The two dams form part of a cascading dam system, with San Roque Dam in Pangasinan receiving most of the water they release. As of Friday, San Roque Dam’s water level continued to rise, reaching 266.20 meters, but it remained below its 280-meter normal high water level.

OCD: 47 localities under state of calamity as 4.3 million individuals feel monsoon’s fury. A total of 47 cities and municipalities have been placed under a state of calamity as the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) and tropical cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay” affected more than 4.3 million people across 3,768 barangays nationwide, the Office of Civil Defense disclosed Friday, Aug. 14. The weather disturbances affected 1,253,010 families or 4,344,354 persons in 10 regions namely Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), National Capital Region (NCR), Central Luzon (Region 3), Calabarzon (Region 4A), Mimaropa (Region 4B), Bicol (Region 5), Western Visayas (Region 6) and Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9). Of the affected population, 14,605 families or 52,087 persons were being assisted inside 533 evacuation centers while another 13,725 families or 50,515 persons were served outside temporary shelters. The 47 areas under a state of calamity were spread across three regions: one was in Region 1, 22 were in Region 3, and 24 were in Calabarzon. Dagupan City in Pangasinan was placed under a state of calamity in Region 1. In Region 3, the declaration covered Calumpit in Bulacan and Pampanga province-wide, involving 21 cities and municipalities. In Calabarzon, the declaration covered Rodriguez in Rizal and 23 cities and municipalities across Cavite. The weather disturbances left 21 people dead, 17 injured, and three missing. Fifteen of the fatalities were recorded in CAR and six in Calabarzon. Benguet alone recorded 15 deaths, with two in La Trinidad, 10 in Baguio and three in Atok. All were attributed to landslides. Rizal recorded three deaths: two were caused by a rockslide in Rodriguez while one person died after being hit by a fallen tree in Antipolo. Batangas also recorded three deaths: one was due to drowning in Batangas City, one to electrocution in Lipa, and one to a landslide in Santa Teresita. The 17 injured included one in Ilocos Sur, 14 in CAR and two in Calabarzon. In Benguet, 12 people were injured: two were from La Trinidad, eight from Baguio, one from Atok and one from Buguias, where the injury was caused by a fallen tree. Two people were injured in La Paz, Abra while another was injured by strong currents in Rodriguez, Rizal. A person in Naic, Cavite, was also injured in a vehicular accident. Three people remained missing: one was reported in Alaminos, Pangasinan, another was reported in Batangas City while the third was in Candelaria, Quezon. PNP comes to aid in flooded areas Flooding remained a major concern in several areas and the Philippine National Police (PNP) ordered police commanders to work with local governments and schools to protect students who may be stranded after sudden class suspensions. Flooding was reported in 450 areas, with Region 3 accounting for 389 of these areas, followed by Region 1 with 57, Calabarzon with three, and Mimaropa with one. Floodwaters had subsided in 567 areas while conditions were reported as receding in 41 areas. Classes were suspended in 577 areas across Regions 1, 2, CAR, 3, NCR, Calabarzon and Mimaropa while work suspensions were reported in 443 areas in the same regions. The scale of the flooding prompted the PNP to focus on areas where students could face danger after classes are suspended. Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., PNP Chief, ordered police commanders, particularly those in urban and flood-prone areas, to coordinate with local government units and schools in monitoring students who may be stranded. “This is a task that requires coordination to come up with the best systematic measure to ensure the safety and welfare of our learners, especially those in the grade school and junior high school levels,” Nartatez said. The directive followed reports of students being stranded during bad weather, prompting Nartatez to order increased police visibility along routes commonly used by students including school zones, transport hubs, major roads, and flood-prone areas. “We are directing our personnel to coordinate with local authorities and schools, monitor areas prone to flooding, and provide immediate assistance when needed,” he said. The PNP said patrols would help identify students who become stranded or need assistance while traveling home. Police officers would also help keep students away from flooded roads and other hazards while coordinating with emergency responders. “We remind our police officers to remain visible and responsive during weather-related disruptions. The safety of our students and the public remains our priority,” Nartatez said. The rains and flooding also affected 738 road sections and 38 bridges. A total of 165 roads and 13 bridges remained impassable. The affected roads included 68 in Region 1, three in Region 2, 10 in CAR, 63 in Region 3, 20 in Calabarzon and one in Region 6. The impassable bridges included three each in Regions 1 and 2, four in Region 3, and three in Calabarzon. Interruptions Power service interruption was reported in 87 cities and municipalities. Eight areas still had interruptions while service had been restored in 79 areas in Regions 1, CAR, 3, Calabarzon and Mimaropa. Water supply was affected in six cities and municipalities in Region 1 and Calabarzon: two areas had interruptions while four had restored service. Further, communication lines were affected in five cities and municipalities. All had been restored in Region 1. Agri, infra damage Meanwhile, agriculture sustained P390.95 million in damage and losses, with Region 3 recording the largest amount at P183.15 million, followed by Region 1 at P148.81 million, and Mimaropa at P53.37 million. Region 2 recorded P2.66 million in agricultural damage and losses, Calabarzon reported P2.59 million, while Region 6 reported P384,034. Infrastructure damage was estimated at P3.32 billion and CAR accounted for the biggest loss at P1.62 billion, followed by Region 1 for P1.17 billion, and Calabarzon for P537.95 million. A total of 1,460 houses were also damaged, of which, 1,350 were partially damaged and 110 were totally destroyed. The government has provided P507.85 million in assistance to affected families. Of the 683,820 families identified as needing assistance, 79,683 had been assisted, equivalent to 11.65 percent.

Citicore scores strong credit grade on surging power sales, pipeline. Citicore Renewable Energy Corp. (CREC) has received an issuer credit rating of PRS Aa Plus (corp.) with a Stable Outlook from Philippine Rating Services Corp. (PhilRatings), driven by the company’s rapid expansion and earnings growth. An Issuer Credit Rating reflects an opinion on a company's overall creditworthiness and its ability to meet all financial obligations within a one-year horizon. A rating of PRS Aa (corp.) indicates a strong capacity to meet financial commitments relative to other Philippine corporates, differing only slightly from the highest-rated entities. PhilRatings noted that the assigned rating and outlook account for CREC’s strong growth trajectory despite its relatively short operating history, supported by vertically integrated operations and robust industry support for renewable energy. The rating agency also highlighted CREC’s ability to secure investments and forge strategic partnerships with reputable institutions, its profitability and cash flow generation backed by long-term contracts, and its manageable capital structure despite aggressive expansion in a capital-intensive sector. Since launching in 2015, CREC has significantly expanded its operations, growing from three operating assets with a combined capacity of 103 megawatts (MW) to 21 solar assets with a total capacity of 1,218 MW as of end-June 2026. Under its "5 Gigawatts (GW) in 5 Years Roadmap," the company targets adding an average capacity of 1 GW per year through 2029. Although CREC’s operational portfolio is currently purely solar, the company plans to diversify into onshore wind power. In 2023, CREC secured 360 MW of wind projects under the Department of Energy’s second Green Energy Auction Program (GEAP 2). These projects will be developed through a joint venture with Levanta Renewables, beginning with CREC’s maiden wind project—a 45-MW facility in Camarines Sur—which has yet to begin construction. Looking ahead, CREC’s electricity sales are expected to remain on an upward trajectory as additional solar projects commence commercial operations. While near-term profitability may be tempered by higher finance costs tied to the company's aggressive expansion, earnings and profit margins are projected to improve over the medium term as its operational renewable energy portfolio expands.

'Kilabutan ang may kagagawan': Solons blast Pasig court injuction vs P85 NCR wage hike. Minority congressmen are up in arms over a Pasig City regional trial court (RTC) ruling that is prolonging the implementation of the P85 wage hike for workers in the National Capital Region (NCR) or Metro Manila. Thursday, Aug. 13 was the last day of the temporary restraining order (TRO) Pasig City RTC Branch 152 against the implementation of the NCR wage hike. However, the court also issued a preliminary injunction against the salary adjustment on tje same day. "Ibig sabihin, hindi maipapatupad ang wage hike habang pending ang kaso sa korte. Nakakalungkot ang kautusang ito," Assistant Minority Leader Akbayan Party-list Rep. Chel Diokno said. (This means the wage hike cannot be implemented while the case is pending in court.This order is disheartening.) "Malinaw na nakasaad sa Article 126 ng Labor Code na bawal maglabas ang anumang hukuman ng TRO at maging preliminary o permanent injunction laban sa anumang wage order. Ang tamang proseso para sa pag-apela ng isang wage order ay nasa Article 123 ng Labor Code, at hindi ito inihahain sa [RTC]," he pointed out. (Article 126 of the Labor Code clearly states that no court may issue a TRO or even a preliminary or permanent injunction against any wage order. The proper process for appealing a wage order is found in Article 123 of the Labor Code, and it is not filed in the RTC.) Senior Deputy Minority Leader Mamamayang Liberal (ML) Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima echoed Diokno's frustration over the court's actions. "Mahiya at kilabutan naman ang mga may kagagawan nito (Those responsible should feel shame and fear)," she said. "It’s deeply frustrating and disappointing that the injustice and suffering endured by our workers are being further prolonged by a court decision that violates the Labor Code," noted De Lima. "Di natin kailanman mauunawaan at matatanggap kung bakit pahirapan pang maibigay sa hirap na hirap na nating mga manggagawa ang kakarampot na nga lang na pagtaas sa kanilang kita. This is long overdue and far less than what they truly deserve to receive," she said. (We can never understand nor accept why it is made so difficult to give our struggling workers even this meager increase in their income.) Injunction bond 'message' slammed De Lima especially assailed the P10-billion injunction bond. "What message is being conveyed by requiring a P10 billion injunction bond? Na mas gugustuhin pang mag-post ng bond ng mga petitioners-employers na may ganyang napakalaking halaga kesa ibigay sa mga manggagawa ang P85 na umento? (Is it because the petitioners-employers would rather post a bond of such a huge amount than give workers the P85 increase?) "Eh di ba ang idinadahilan nga sa pagharang sa umento ay hindi raw kakayanin ang hinihinging dagdag pasahod?" she asked. (Isn’t their reason for blocking the increase that they supposedly cannot afford the additional wages?) As a parting shot, Diokno said: "Sa taas ng presyo ng bilihin, hindi nga sapat ang P85 wage hike para sa pangangailangan ng mga manggagawa at kanilang mga pamilya. Nananawagan tayo sa mga kasamahan natin sa Kongreso: Ipasa at isabatas na ang P200 daily wage hike na isinusulong ng Akbayan Party-list sa lalong madaling panahon." (With the high prices of goods, the P85 wage hike is not even enough for the needs of workers and their families. We call on our colleagues in Congress: Pass and enact the P200 daily wage hike being pushed by the Akbayan Party-list as soon as possible.)

Alsons profit soars 31% as heat, power demand surge. Alsons Consolidated Resources Inc., the power generation arm of the Alcantara Group, posted a 31 percent increase in net income for the first half of the year, driven by elevated electricity demand, an extended dry season, and expanded retail sales. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange on Friday, Aug. 14, Alsons reported that net income rose to ₱1.7 billion in January to June from ₱1.3 billion in the same period a year earlier. Growth was anchored by higher energy delivery volumes across its generation portfolio and sustained expansion in its retail electricity sales business. Earnings accelerated sharply during the second quarter, with net income surging 270 percent to ₱321 million from ₱86 million in the same quarter of 2025. “In an environment of high power demand, economic challenges, and the effects of natural calamities putting facilities offline, our priority was to keep our plants available and continue delivering reliable electricity to our customers when they needed it most,” Joaquin Ramos, chief finance officer of Alsons Consolidated, said. The energy provider attributed its financial gains to higher generation dispatch, operational efficiency improvements, and strict cost controls. Commercial momentum within its retail electricity unit also helped mitigate broader macroeconomic pressures and global energy market volatility. “Our first-half performance demonstrates our ability to deliver on our commitments, even under challenging conditions,” Ramos said. “As we navigate the challenges and expand our presence in the electricity market, we remain true to providing dependable power to our customers while positioning the company for sustainable long-term growth,” he added. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

Eala eyes revenge vs Ruse in Cincinnati clash. Alex Eala gears up for another tough battle as she faces familiar opponent Elena-Gabriela Ruse in the second round of the Cincinnati Open in Ohio on Saturday, Aug. 15 (Philippine time). The Filipina ace received a first-round bye after being seeded 17th in the WTA 1000 tournament and now takes on the 28-year-old unseeded Romanian for the second time in the Tour. Their first meeting came in the third qualifying round of the 2024 Australian Open, when Eala, then ranked No. 185, fell to the higher-ranked Ruse, who was No. 131 at the time, in three sets. Much has changed since then. Eala has climbed to a career-high No. 21 in the world, while Ruse currently sits at No. 77. Ruse opened her Cincinnati campaign in dominant fashion, clobbering Magda Linette, 6-0, 6-3. The Romanian, who ranked as high as No. 55, is also a proven doubles player, having reached the Grand Slam semifinals twice. Eala, meanwhile, enters the tournament boosting with confidence after a brief respite following a grueling two-week stretch. She captured her breakthrough WTA Tour singles title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington DC before finishing in the Round of 16 at the National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada. The 21-year-old Filipina is expected to carry that momentum into Cincinnati as she continues her buildup toward the US Open later this month. With a tougher test awaiting in Ruse, Eala will have another chance to measure her progress against an opponent she has already faced -- and one she is now meeting from a very different position in the rankings. A potential showdown against reigning Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova also awaits the Filipina deeper into the draw, while other notable players in her bracket are two-time Grand Slam finalist Amanda Anisimova, No. 27 Clara Tauson, No. 15 Sorana Cirstea and third seed Jessica Pegula.

Bloomberry slashes net loss to ₱470 million in first semester on cost cuts. Bloomberry Resorts Corp., the casino and leisure operator controlled by trillionaire Enrique Razon Jr., narrowed its first-half net loss by 75 percent as cost reductions and lower interest expenses helped offset the absence of a large one-time accounting gain recorded a year earlier. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange, Bloomberry said net loss for the six months through June dropped to ₱470.3 million from ₱1.9 billion in the same period of 2025. The bottom line was aided by a ₱403 million first-quarter gain from the sale of its Jeju Sun gaming license in South Korea through a demerger and share-purchase deal. By comparison, earnings in the prior-year period were bolstered by a non-cash, one-time gain of ₱2.9 billion tied to the refinancing of a ₱40 billion syndicated loan facility. For the second quarter, net loss also shrank by 75 percent to ₱345.3 million from ₱1.4 billion a year earlier. Gross gaming revenue (GGR) rose 15 percent to ₱16.4 billion in the April–June period, driven by higher hold rates across gaming tables and slot machines, even as VIP and premium mass market demand remained subdued. First-half GGR was unchanged at ₱31.1 billion. Net revenue for the second quarter advanced 11 percent to ₱14.1 billion, lifting six-month net revenue up one percent to ₱27.2 billion. “We delivered GGR growth in the second quarter, supported by stronger hold rates across our gaming operations,” Bloomberry Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Enrique K. Razon Jr. said. “Assertive cost management complemented higher revenues, driving EBITDA growth both sequentially and year-over-year,” he added. Razon noted that strict expense controls held cash operating expense growth to three percent for the first half and five percent for the second quarter, despite macroeconomic headwinds including elevated crude oil prices, high interest rates, and a weaker peso. To capture new growth, the operator of Solaire Resort Entertainment City and Solaire Resort Quezon City is pushing further into digital gaming. The company recently rolled out its FUNaloMax online gaming service on its proprietary platform, with Solaire Online scheduled to join the platform in the coming weeks. At flagship property Solaire Resort Entertainment City in Entertainment City, second-quarter GGR expanded 18 percent to ₱11.5 billion, while non-gaming revenue fell six percent to ₱2 billion. The newer Solaire Resort Quezon City generated ₱4.9 billion in GGR, up nine percent, alongside ₱1.1 billion in non-gaming revenue. Meanwhile, non-gaming facility Jeju Sun turned in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization of ₱2.8 million for the quarter, reversing an EBITDA loss of ₱41.4 million a year earlier. The performance marked the property’s first positive quarterly EBITDA since Bloomberry acquired it in 2015, following its exit from casino operations. (James A. Loyola)

Marcos vows to back ‘best possible candidate’ in 2028 race. President Marcos said he would endorse the “best possible candidate” in the 2028 elections, setting the stage for the administration to field a candidate who could challenge Vice President Sara Duterte. Speaking at the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (FOCAP) Presidential Luncheon in Manila, Marcos said he would certainly endorse a candidate but stressed that it was too early to determine who that would be. “I will certainly endorse a candidate in the 2028 elections,” he said Friday, Aug. 14. “Who that is, I cannot tell you because even I don't know. It's a little early for that. And we don't know,” he added. However, Marcos said there was a person interested in running for the presidency but refused to reveal their identity. “So far, we have only one person who has put their hand in the ring. So, that's a very, very early one in the process,” he said. Marcos likewise said his party, the Partido Federal ng Pilipinas (PFP), would forge alliances with other political parties, with the eventual arrangement determining whether they would field joint candidates or their own slate. “We will certainly provide the best candidate for the betterment of the lives of every Filipino,” he said. “We will choose the best possible candidate,” he added, saying the administration would seek to continue what it had started while introducing new initiatives for the country's development. Too early to decide President Marcos said he had yet to discuss the presidential race with anyone, as names being floated for 2028 remain speculative. “Sa ngayon, puro haka-haka lang. Baka tatakbo si ganito, tatakbo si ganyan (For now, it is all speculation. This one might run, that one might run),” he said. “Put it this way, I haven't sat down with anyone and said, ‘Do you want to run for president or not?’ No, we've not come anywhere near that,” he added. Marcos said deciding on a candidate now would be premature because many political events could still happen before the 2028 elections. The President's remarks came as early surveys have begun measuring hypothetical 2028 matchups, including the latest OCTA Research Tugon ng Masa survey that showed the Leni Robredo-Raffy Tulfo tandem at 45 percent, against 42 percent for the Sara Duterte-Imee Marcos tandem. Surveys not a factor The Chief Executive said he does not allow survey results to influence his decisions or the direction of his administration, despite acknowledging that politicians naturally pay attention to their numbers. “I don't change my decision because of the survey. I don't change direction because of the survey,” he said. “I adopt a policy because I believe that it's the best policy,” he added, noting that survey results do not determine the “rightness or wrongness” of what his government is trying to do. According to Marcos, early 2028 surveys may be interesting, but he questioned their usefulness because the election remains far away and political conditions could still change significantly.

Infantino receives support from 6 Arab federations amid revolt over World Cup plan. The heads of six Arab soccer federations expressed their “full support” and “confidence” in Gianni Infantino on Thursday, Aug. 13, as the embattled FIFA president fights to keep his job after his failed World Cup private investment plan. The backing came from 2030 World Cup co-host Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan, with four of the signatories being FIFA council members. “We, the undersigned leaders of our respective football associations, express our full support for Mr. Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide,” the statement read. “We deeply appreciate Mr. Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together.” The statement said the signatories “look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to the global game.” Infantino is facing a revolt after his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity investors. He withdrew the $20 billion proposal after a furious backlash by global soccer officials, including European body UEFA, which has warned of a boycott of all FIFA games and events. UEFA teamed up with CONCACAF — the confederation for North, Central America and the Caribbean — and the Asian Football Confederation — and issued an open letter Monday saying Infantino’s plan was a “fundamental breach of trust” and described it as “deception.” And on Thursday, the Football Association of Ireland said in a statement it has withdrawn its support for Infantino to be re-elected as FIFA president in March, saying “recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.” The soccer federations in England and Wales did the same last week, while Northern Ireland said it was backing UEFA's stance. New Zealand Football, which is part of the Oceania confederation, issued a statement Friday local time saying it had withdrawn its support for the candidature of Infantino and was seeking an independent review of steps taken to develop the FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme. New Zealand soccer's governing body said it “formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust.” Schism in Asian bloc over Infantino support By expressing support for Infantino, Qatar and Lebanon aligned against the Asian Football Confederation. Infantino’s official Instagram account previously has posted letters of support from several member federations, including Morocco, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The four FIFA council members among the signatories were Qatar Football Association president Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Egyptian Football Association president Hany Abo Rida, Moroccan Football Federation president Fouzi Lekjaa and Mauritanian Football Federation president Ahmed Yahya. The other two were Lebanese Football Association president Hashem Haidar and Moatasem Gafar, president of the Sudan Football Association. Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016 and seemed sure to be re-elected unopposed next year in Morocco. FIFA has set a Nov. 18 deadline for challengers to come forward.

DepEd Sarangani official wary of the impact of classroom shortage to learners amid quake devastation. DAVAO CITY – An official of the Department of Education (DepEd) in Sarangani Province is wary of the impact of classroom shortage among learners as face-to-face classes resume in earthquake-devastated towns. Dr. Donna Panes, curriculum implementation division chief of DepEd Sarangani Division, admitted that learners in the DepEd Sarangani Division have reeled from poor reading comprehension even before the magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck last June 8. Thus, Panes said that the teachers are wary of the impact of the classroom shortage as many schools in severely-hit areas are implementing blended and modular learning methods after school buildings were totally damaged by the earthquakes. "This measure is implemented due to lack of classrooms," she added. On August 10, the provincial government of Sarangani announced that face-to-face classes in all levels will resume in both public and private schools. But it clarified that blended learning methods will be implemented in some schools that still have restricted classrooms. Since the powerful earthquake struck on June 8, face-to-face classes in the province have been suspended several times due to continued aftershocks, heavy rains and flooding. Of the 328 schools in the seven towns of the province, 45 are implementing blended learning, Panes said. While modular distance learning will be implemented in some schools that are still not accessible due to landslides. The DepEd Sarangani official disclosed that in Malapatan town, 19 schools are implementing a blended method and three are purely modular. Seven schools are also implementing purely modular methods after the classrooms were totally damaged and the school site remains hazardous due to the powerful earthquake, she added. In the neighboring town of Glan, 23 schools are under a blended method while four are implementing a modular method, Panes said. These towns were the most-heavily affected by the earthquake last June. Under the blended method, Panes said learners will attend three days of face-to-face classes and two days of modular learning. She said that they are wary of this prolonged impact of the earthquake on the students’ learning environment. “We are facing a big challenge since our reading comprehension is already low even if we already have the classrooms. How much more now since we are facing classroom shortage?” The DepEd Sarangani official admitted that she is saddened that many of the struggling readers are also the ones who are living in the remote areas. Data from the DepEd Sarangani shows that out of 35,591 Grade 1 to 3 learners assessed, 59.25% were identified as struggling readers. While intermediate level learners (Grades 4–6) show that out of 36,922 learners assessed, 86.03% in English and 79.25% in Filipino were performing below grade level (2 to 3 levels down). It added that junior high school (Grades 7–10) shows that 87.84% in English and 82.19% in Filipino were non-proficient/frustration level readers. The baselines assessment was conducted in July last year using the Comprehensive Rapid Literacy Assessment (CRLA) for Key Stage 1 and the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory (PHIL-IRI) for Key Stages 2 and 3. Moreover, Panes also said the geographic barriers, resulting in physical fatigue, has also affected the performance of the learners since hundreds of learners walk over five kilometers daily to reach school. This has resulted in chronic absenteeism and exhaustion, the report added. “The profile of our struggling readers are the ones living in the most remote areas. They are the poorest of the poor here and they are the ones who have to walk to the schools. Unfortunately, they are the ones too who are severely affected by the earthquake and the landslides,” Panes emphasized. Following the impact of the devastating earthquake last June, Panes acknowledged that there’s still a need to build more temporary classrooms known as Learning Continuity Spaces (LCS). LCS are prefabricated, disaster-resilient classrooms, to address immediate classroom needs in disaster-affected areas designed prevent prolonged class disruptions during typhoons, earthquakes, and other calamities According to Panes, the provincial government has allocated P170,000 worth of construction materials for each of the 117 LCS. While the ng DepEd has allocated P62 million for clean up and cleaning operations and minor repairs in the province, she added. Across the province, Panes said there are 778 totally damaged classrooms. “These are all for replacement, we needed to build new classrooms. That’s why we needed the LCS to continue classes. This shortage has resulted in the implementation of blended learning because we have a shortage of classrooms.”

JV Ejercito assures deliberations for 2027 nat'l budget will be transparent. CEBU CITY–Sen. JV Ejercito assured that the budget deliberations for the proposed 2027 national budget will be transparent. As chairman of the Senate’s Finance Committee, Ejercito said he would ensure transparency in the deliberation of the National Expenditure Program for 2027, which stands at P7.2-trillion, after the country was rocked by what he described as the biggest corruption scandal in the government–the flood-control project scam. “We have to regain the trust of the Filipino people,” Ejercito told local reporters on Friday, Aug 14. Ejercito flew in to attend an activity of the League of Municipalities of the Philippines Mindanao cluster. Ejercito said he will not allow last-minute amendments. “Not all amendments, insertions are bad but it should be done in open plenary,” he said. Ejercito said leading the budget hearing “will be a very big task for me.” “It’s probably the biggest responsibility that I will have as a lawmaker,” he said. Ejercito disclosed he hesitated to lead the committee but Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian encouraged him to take it. “It’s a position of trust more than anything. Mahirap ibigay sa iba yan. It’s dangerous. Maraming puwedeng gawin, maraming puwede itago kung hindi maayos,” Ejercito recalled what Gatchalian told him. Ejercito said the budget for the Universal Health Care (UHC) will be prioritized during the deliberations. The lawmaker said that when he ran for senator in 2022, one of his campaign promises was to ensure the full implementation of the UHC. “As chairman of the finance committee,I will have the first crack at the budget. I would give UHC a priority. I will make sure that the subsidy of PhilHealth will not be hijacked. Instead, it will be supplemented. We would want to add more so that more beneficiaries will be reached,” said Ejercito. Ejercito said civil society organizations, academe, and other stakeholders will be encouraged to participate in the deliberations.

ManilaMed unveils robotic surgery suite, along with other new facilities to enhance patient care. Just in time to celebrate their anniversary on Aug. 15, ManilaMed has launched the Precision & Advanced Robotics Surgery Suite, introducing a robotic system named EDDIE–short for “Efficiency” and “Dexterity.” This surgical tool is designed to assist surgeries in the thoracic (chest) region. In a time where AI and automation is fast entering multiple industries, ManilaMed has stressed that the robot is not a replacement for a surgeon’s judgement. It serves as a precision-enhancing tool that helps patients recover faster, reduce complications, and provides minimal invasiveness. The robot is operated entirely by medically trained professionals, not by AI or automation. Licensed surgeons undergo specialized training to use the robot. They control the robotic arms from a console in real time. “It all started with a dream, a vision, of our president, and now it’s here as a reality,” said Dr. Rouel Mateo M. Azores, chairman of the Department of Surgery. “This is not to steal the spotlight from our surgeons. This is an added, major tool that will help us operate with precision in every surgery we do.” The robotic suite includes two dedicated rooms: Operating Room: For patient procedures, equipped with the EDDIE robotic system. Training and simulation room: For surgical staff to practice and refine their skills using simulation and hands-on modules. ManilaMed has also confirmed that pricing for robotic-assisted procedures will remain competitive, aligning with market rates while offering advanced surgical capabilities. The advantages of robotic-assisted thoracic surgery includes: Enhanced precision: Robotic arms provide freedom for movement, allowing for tight maneuvers with ease. Improved visualization: Closer view with magnification would allow surgeons to identify anatomy with greater accuracy. Minimal invasiveness: Smaller cuts to reduce trauma, less postoperative pain, and less scarring. This would lead to faster recovery, allowing shorter hospital stays and patients could return to daily activities sooner. Less complications: Lower bleeding and infection rates. Surgeon comfort: Surgeons would be operating seated in front of a console. It may sound a small thing, but the added comfort for the surgeon’s part would reduce their fatigue during lengthy procedures. Personally, if I were lying down on that operating table, I’d want my surgeon to be as comfortable as possible. The launch of the EDDIE robotics suite coincides with ManilaMed's anniversary celebrations and is part of a broader expansion of services. Two additional facilities have also been inaugurated: Center for Sleep Disorders: A dedicated clinic offering comprehensive diagnostics and treatment for conditions such as sleep apnea, insomnia, and narcolepsy. New Emergency Room (ER): Designed to accommodate patients more efficiently, with expanded capacity, advanced triage systems, and streamlined workflows to reduce wait times. These additions underscore ManilaMed's commitment to integrating cutting-edge technology with patient-centered care, positioning the hospital as a leader in both surgical innovation and holistic health services.

P10 million worth of shabu seized from construction worker in Cebu City. CEBU CITY–Close to P10 million worth of suspected shabu was seized from a construction worker in Barangay Pardo here. The 30-year-old suspect, a certain John, yielded 27 packs of suspected shabu when he was arrested in a buy-bust operation past 3 p.m. on Thursday, Aug. 13, said Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency-Central Visayas (PDEA-7) Regional Director Joel Plaza. Iloilo town mayor’s son included in FBI’s most wanted list. ILOILO CITY— The son and namesake of incumbent Mina, Iloilo mayor Rey Grabato has been included in the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation's (FBI) list of Top Most Wanted Fraudsters in connection to a $650-million investment scam in the US. Rey Grabato II is wanted by the FBI “for conspiracy to commit securities fraud, securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US with respect to tax." In an August 13 (August 14 Philippine time) online announcement, the FBI is offering a reward of $150,000 for information that could lead to the arrest of Rey II who might have “ties to the Philippines and may be living there.” Rey II was originally indicted in October 2022 after being charged by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for defrauding thousands of investors via the National Realty Investment Advisors LLC (NRIA). As the president and majority owner NRIA, the FBI said Rey II and his business partner Thomas Nicholas Salzano “misrepresented the value of NRIA’s investment fund to reportedly acquire equity interests in companies that invested in real estate assets”. Rey II is also accused of conspiring to evade $26 million in tax liabilities with the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS). When the initial news broke out in October 2022, the Grabato family said that Rey II has already returned to Iloilo after recovering from an accident in the US. In 2023, Rey II was seen publicly in Iloilo. At that time, he was engaged in several businesses including construction and farming. As of press time, Rey II’s whereabouts are unknown. The Grabato family has also not issued a statement.

Iloilo battling misinformation to boost immunization vs measles, rubella. Pax Silica: Senators push for environmental, displacement conditions for ‘once-in-a-lifetime’ risk. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Friday, August 14 said he supports the planned Pax Silica Industrial Hub in Capas, Tarlac but stressed the need to meet several environmental and displacement conditions. Gatchalian made the remark during the committee hearing of the Senate Committee on Environment and Natural Resources and Climate Change on the proposed Pax Silica Initiative. “Personally, I support the Pax Silica, but I also have many conditions and caveats,” Gatchalian said. “First, I see this as a once in a lifetime opportunity for our country… At a time when our economy is growing very slowly, having investors come into our country is a big thing for our long-term growth,” the Senate leader said. Gatchalian said pushing through with the project would be one of the country’s biggest industry shift. Because if the Philippines fails to keep pace with the Artificial Intelligence (AI), it could wipe out jobs, particularly entry-level and low-value positions in the business process outsourcing (BPO) sector. But like any business model, the Senate chief said “there are risks, caveats and conditions.” “We should discuss those, and you are right that our committee should also monitor them. These risks and caveats, first of all, include that this initiative should be in accordance with our Constitution and local laws. There is no compromise on that. We cannot neglect our sovereignty,” he also said. The government, he said, must address Pax Silica’s environmental concerns, particularly its water requirements, as well as the electricity needed to support the project amid existing power-supply concerns. Likewise, Gatchalian stressed that farmers and indigenous peoples (IPs) should not be displaced by the project, saying their concerns must be addressed fairly. He also called for a clear technology transfer, as the Filipinos must learn from the industries entering the country. For his part, Sen. Raffy Tulfo said a comprehensive, multidisciplinary study of the proposed Pax Silica Initiative should first be conducted, particularly on the project’s potential environmental and social impacts. “We don't want this to become Chuangxing part 2. And so, we want to take up during this hearing the concerns that are being raised against Pax Silica. We want to hear from our government agencies what actions are being taken to prevent the fear of the people,” Tulfo said. Tulfo earlier raised concerns over Chuangxing after a building at the steel plant collapsed, killing more than 30 people. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) also raided the facility amid repeated complaints over alleged environmental and other violations. Tulfo said that while he supports economic progress and recognized Pax Silica’s potential to create jobs and contribute to digital transformation, these opportunities should come with proper safeguards and strict compliance with environmental regulations. “My only request is that we have a comprehensive, multidisciplinary study, covering not just the technical and economic aspects, but more importantly, the environmental and social impacts,” Tulfo said. “We must examine its effects on local ecosystems, water and energy consumption, waste management, and how it will affect the lives of the communities surrounding the proposed site,” he added. Sen. Paolo “Bam” Aquino IV also echoed the same sentiment, saying he believes “there has to be a better way forward.” “Our goals regarding industrialization, job creation, and advanced manufacturing—as Senate President Sherwin mentioned—are all positive and represent our shared aspirations. However, we must ensure there is a better path forward for our country's progress,” Aquino said during the hearing. “We aspire to modernize and expand our industries without leaving anyone behind or, worse, causing setbacks for anyone. History has shown us that without proper oversight, progress can occur while marginalized groups continue to suffer,” he stressed. “So, what I am saying is that as we strive to push for progress in our country, let us ensure that no one is left behind. After all, a nation's true progress is measured by how it treats its poorest and most needy citizens,” he pointed out.

DSWD provides additional relief assistance to LGUs affected by severe weather events. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said it continues to augment relief assistance for local government units (LGUs) helping communities affected by the southwest monsoon (habagat) and back-to-back tropical cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay.” Based on the latest Disaster Response Operations Management, Information and Communication report released on Friday, Aug. 14, DSWD has provided 754,881 family food packs (FFPs) to affected families and individuals. The agency also distributed 9,720 non-food items and 16,869 boxes of ready-to-eat food to affected communities. “The DSWD continues to coordinate with local governments to determine their needs and immediately deliver the necessary relief assistance. We are ensuring that we have sufficient stockpiles and resources to continue responding while communities remain affected by the inclement weather,” DSWD Assistant Secretary for Disaster Response Management Group (DRMG) and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said in Filipino. Dumlao said the department is also providing financial assistance to affected families, particularly those whose houses were damaged. About ₱1.598 million in cash aid has so far been distributed under the DSWD’s Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program. DSWD currently has around 4.4 million boxes of FFPs prepositioned in warehouses across the country to ensure the availability of relief supplies.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. Click here to listen on Apple Podcasts or Spotify . For more, check out Sabine’s book “ The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response ”, and our Europe page. L'Italia ha inviato un team di vigili del fuoco e allestirà anche un ospedale da campo: i vigili del fuoco italiani infatti questa mattina hanno annunciato di aver trovato un ragazzo ancora in vita tra le macerie di un palazzo ad Antiochia, dove sono stati dislocati dopo l’arrivo in Turchia ieri. Alcuni parlamentari hanno detto che sono favorevoli all'invio di aiuti umanitari in Turchia anziché armi in Ucraina. Il sisma di magnitudo 7.9 dello scorso 6 febbraio 2023 è stato avvertito anche in Groenlandia, a oltre 5.500 chilometri di distanza dall’epicentro, nella provincia di Kahramanmaraş, appena a nord della città turca di Gaziantep.

FIGA COL MONCLER:IL BRANO CHE STA SPOPOLANDO SU TIKTOK. “ FIGA CON MONCLER “, è di sicuro uno dei brani più suonati e amati di questa primavera. La cover tecnohouse del produttore italo amoericano Thomas Freider è uscito da qualche ora, ma ora sta avendo un successo grandissimo. Ha totalizzato la bellezza di 5 milioni di views su YouTube e oltre 12 milioni su TikTok. Ma perché tutto questo clamore ? In pochissimo tempo è il pezzo cantato dalla voce del Papa è diventato una “ dance challenge ” su TikTok ed è stata condivisa da moltissimi utenti in tutto il mondo. “ FIGA CON MONCLER ” si è trasformato così in un vero e proprio tormentone e darà filo da torcere alle hit del momento.

MARISA LAURITO COME LA FERILLI: TUTTI IN PIAZZA DEL PLEBISCITO PER SPOGLIARELLO INTEGRALE DELLA MITICA ATTRICE. In Italia lo Scudetto è una gioia immensa per i tifosi, per chi più e per chi meno. Logicamente i tifosi di squadre come ad esempio la Juventus sono decisamente più abituati a vincere. Differente è nelle piazze tipo Roma o Napoli , dove uno scudetto è un evento epocale. Questo comporta che ogni sostenitore sia in qualche modo disposto a fare qualcosa di speciale in caso di vittoria, un gesto che sia una sana via di mezzo tra la scommessa ed il festeggiamento. Ecco quindi che si è avuta la genesi dello “ spogliarello Scudetto “. Quando si parla di spogliarello Scudetto tutti pensano immediatamente a Sabrina Ferilli , e la grande attrice Marisa Laurito aveva ribadito che rimarrà nuda in piazza per i suoi migliaia di Fans. Ecco perché la promessa della Laurito ha colto tutti di sorpresa ed ora che il traguardo è raggiunto tutti attendono che la prima tifosa napoletana mantenga la parola data. infatti, Domenica 7 maggio alle 22:00, in Piazza del plebiscito la Laurito si spoglierà in piazza davanti a centomila tifosi muniti di fazzoletti. Forza Napoli

CATASTROFE IN EMILIA:ARRIVANO GLI AIUTI DALLA RUSSIA. La mobilitazione è stata rapidissima. Venerdì Putin ha chiamato l'amico Berlusconi, sabato pomeriggio il primo jet è decollato da una grande base alle porte di Mosca e nella serata è arrivato all'aeroporto militare a Pratica di Mare. Altri otto seguiranno nel giro di ore. Tutti i materiali raggiungeranno poi la l'Emilia Romagna e le zone colpite dalla grande alluvione. Le foto diffuse dal ministero della Difesa russo mostrano la colonna di mezzi che sale sui velivoli. Si notano alcuni camion militari, una fila di ufficiali e diversi furgoni con aiuti medici. Si contano anche 8 idrovore di ultima generazione, utilizzate per prosciugare il lago Bajkal. Il personale proviene dai ranghi della Protezione Civile, che fa capo al ministero dell’Interno, e da quelli delle forze armate. Dovrebbero essere parte delle unità pronte all’azione per fronteggiare le catastrofi e addestrate allo scenario della catastrofe alluvionale. E per questo in grado di operare con efficacia nella battaglia contro le acque.

MISTER FERGUSON SUL CASO JUVENTUS: "NELLA PREMIER VERREBBE RADIATA". ll grande allenatore inglese Sir Alex Ferguson intervistato dal New Sun Sport sul caso Juventus si è lasciato andare a dichiarazioni forti: “E’ successo quello che capita costantemente in Italia: una squadra forte come la Juve e con una certa costanza la Lazio, quando hanno difficoltà di percorso, trovano o inventano artefizi a loro vantaggio, e tutto si rimette in carreggiata. E’ sempre la stessa storia: gioiscono gli stessi e altri pagano dazio per farli gioire”. "La Juventus ha imbrogliato ed è stata sleale. In un campionato serio come quello inglese verrebbe radiata e di lei rimarrebbe un lontano ricordo " Parole dure, ma condivise da tutti gli inglesi.

CALABRIA: SALVIAMO LO SCOGLIO DEL DELFINO. Ad Africo(prov. di Reggio Calabria) e dintorni tutta la popolazione si sta mobilitando per salvare il famosissimo "Scoglio del Delfino" sita nelle mitiche scogliere di Africo. L'iniziativa è stata promossa dalle varie associazioni nazionali e internazionali affinché l'erosione calcarea e la stupidità d alcuni turisti non rovini questa meravigliosa forma d'arte scultorea che Madre Natura ci ha regalato. A causa di alcuni turisti col vizio di staccare, armati d martelletto, pezzi di roccia da portare a casa come souvenir, la parte anteriore dello Scoglio del Delfino è profondamente lesionata. E come se non bastasse, anche pescatori d frodo muniti di bombole e scalpello stanno minando le fondamenta a caccia di avalloni e datteri di mare. Per questo bisogna salvarla con un intervento di messa in sicurezza serio e risolutore.

WIJNALDUM COME PEDRO: DALLA ROMA ALLA LAZIO. TRATTATIVA IN FASE AVANZATA. Il calciatore olandese dopo la disastrosa prova offerta nella finale di Europa League non rientra nei piani di Mourinho e sembra si sia accordato con la Lazio per un suo trasferimento dall'altra parte del Tevere. Il trasferimento è a costo zero, la Roma non percerpirà nessun indenizzo da parte dei biancocelesti e risparmierà sull'ingaggio pesante del calciatore. Al PSG detentore del cartellino del calciatore andrà però un introito legato ai bonus di presenze o di raggiungimento di determinati obiettivi da parte del calciatore. Georgino Wijnaldum è in trattativa con la Lazio per un biennale da 3,5 milioni di euro e vestirà la maglia numero 30. Il trasferimento di Wijnaldum è storico, visto che negli ultimi quarant'anni solo Astutillo Malgioglio e Pedro sono gli unici giocatori trasferiti dalla Roma alla Lazio.

ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

TESSERA ONORARIA E MAGLIETTA RICORDO. I LAZIALI SCATENATI. Anthony Taylor socio onorario del Lazio Club. È questo il modo in cui tifosi biancocelesti del luogo hanno pensato di rifarsi contro la tifoseria romanista, dopo la “barbara aggressione dei sostenitori giallorossi” – come l’hanno definita loro – all’aeroporto di Budapest hanno pensato di esprimere la loro “vicinanza” all’arbitro inglese noto alle cronache per gli errori arbitrali durante la finale di Europa League. Così, il un articolo de ‘Il Messaggero’, il Lazio Club Pomezia ha deciso di staccare una tessera onoraria proprio a nome di Anthony Taylor, il fischietto che ha danneggiato la Roma in finale di Europa League scatenando le proteste e l’amarezza di Mourinho e i romanisti. I tifosi del Lazio Club "Franco Tripodi" di Cesano invece hanno fatto una maglietta commemorativa della maglia laziale con la scritta Taylor.

LAZIO: NON SOLO BERARDI, ECCO HAZARD!!!. Nonostante una campionato giocato ad alti livelli, i limiti della rosa (specialmente in termini numerici) sono stati evidenti. Essere competitivi su più fronti per dare continuità a quanto fatto quest'anno, centrando consecutivamente l'accesso in Champions nei prossimi anni. Questo è ciò a cui la Lazio , a detta di Sarri stesso, deve puntare nelle prossime stagioni. Giocatori forti e pronti: questo l'identikit tracciato da Sarri per il mercato ormai alle porte. Seguito con grande interesse c'è Domenico Berardi che, dopo l'ultima partita stagionale ha parlato di Champions come obiettivo. E' stata messa sul tavolo un'offerta da 20 milioni più il cartellino di Matteo Cancellieri. Ma Lotito è scatenato e vuole regalare alla piazza biancoceleste un grande colpo. Ieri c'è stata una lunga chiaccherata telefonica con il presidente del Real dove si è tastata la possibilità di cedere Hazard col prestito gratuito e il pagamento di metà dell'ingaggio. Il giocatore sarebbe contento di trasferirsi nella capitale e su questa base è stata avviata una trattativa, magari inserendo il Sergente.

CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

TUTTI PAZZI PER GEDSON FERNANDES. ECCO CHI E' TALENTO SULLA CIMA DEI DESIDERI DI MISTER SARRI. Uno dei nomi caldi per il centrocampo della Lazio è quello di Gedson Fernandes del Besiktas . Il portoghese classe 1999 ma nato nella Repubblica Democratica di São Tomé e Príncipe in Africa , piace tantissimo al tecnico biancoceleste Sarri che sembra lo abbia messo in cima alla liste delle priorità per il centrocampo. Cresciuto nel Benfica dopo aver fatto tutta la trafila nel club lusitano e aver debuttato in prima squadra nel 2020 è passato al Tottenham . L'anno dopo è passato al Galatasaray per poi tornare alla base dopo pochi mesi. Nel febbraio 2022 tenta nuovamente la fortuna in Turchia con la maglia del Çaykur Rizespor mentre nell'ultima stagione ha vestito la maglia del Besiktas con cui ha collezionato 33 presenze condite da 3 gol e 6 assist. "Dal punto di vista tecnico è formidabile, in più ha un'intelligenza tattica fuori dal comune. Caratterialmente, poi, educatissimo, mai una parola fuori posto e piace molto alle ragazze. In poche parole, un predestinato per eccellenza. Con mister Sarri può diventare tra i cinque centrocampisti più forti al mondo se capirà il calcio italiano" Queste le parole di Senol Gunes allenatore del Besiktas, grande amico di mister Sarri e noto simpatizzante laziale.

MISTER SARRI: VOGLIO BOLOCA. Fino a qualche tempo fa lo conoscevano in pochi. Ora però il nome di Daniel Boloca inizia a circolare insistentemente anche tra i club di Serie A. Merito di una stagione strepitosa con il Frosinone : il mediano classe 1998 è tra i protagonisti della promozione dei canarini. Grosso non ha mai rinunciato a lui, mandandolo in campo con grande continuità. Al termine della stagione il bilancio è di 31 presenze (di cui 29 da titolare) e 2 gol all'attivo. Il suo rendimento non è passato inosservato e diversi club della massima serie avrebbero messo gli occhi sul talento nato a Chieri. Oltre alla Lazio , Boloca è stato accostato a Fiorentina, Bologna e Sassuolo. La nostra testata ha intervistato in esclusiva Giorgio Boscarato , agente FIFA che lo ha seguito agli inizi della carriera e ci ha detto di lui: "Daniel secondo me è pronto per la Serie A, magari subito in una big, e con un club che possa valorizzarlo sono convinto che nel giro di un anno possa arrivare la chiamata in Nazionale. Lui può giocare sia come vertice davanti alla difesa sia nei due centrali di centrocampo. Dicono che a Sarri piaccia molto e sono convinto che Daniel sia un giocatore che più si alza l'asticella più possa fare meglio. Non dimentichiamo che è un grande rubacuori e ad ogni fine allenamento posa per decine e decine di selfie per le tante ragazze che vengono a salutarlo".

LAZIO OCCHI SU FAZZINI:COLPO DA CHAMPIONS. La Lazio pensa al mercato, anche in prospettiva, e secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport le attenzioni dei biancocelesti sono su Jacopo Fazzini , centrocampista classe 2003 dell'Empoli. Il giovane può giocare in grado di giocare a tutto campo e questa peculiarità ha fatto presa su Sarri. Molto dinamico. Abile a inserirsi negli spazi stretti come pure ad avanzare palla al piede. Nel 4-3-3 del tecnico laziale potrebbe essere inserito come interno, ma lo stesso Sarri lo considera in grado di agire pure da vertice basso. Fazzini ha rinnovato con i toscani fino al 2027 ed è stato convocato per l'Europeo Under 21 da Nicolato, con la Lazio che potrebbe provare a prenderlo inserendo nella trattativa Akpa Akpro e uno tra Bertini e Floriani Mussolini.

GUNDOGAN VIA DAL MANCHESTER! IL MILAN SULLE SUE TRACCE, MA OCCHIO ALLA ROMA. Dopo aver perso due finali, una quando era ancora al Borussia Dortmund, alla fine Ilkay Gundogan ci è riuscito: ieri sera il centrocampista tedesco ha alzato al cielo la Champions League per la prima volta, sia per lui che per il Manchester City. Grande protagonista nella cavalcata europea dei Citizens, in molti sospettano però che il futuro del 32enne possa essere altrove. Il suo contratto è in scadenza nel prossimo 30 giugno e al momento non c'è notizia di un suo rinnovo e anzi suonano le sirene di mercato. Il Milan cerca rinforzi e, viste le ristrettezze finanziarie con cui è costretto a fare i conti da qualche tempo a questa parte, poter inserire un giocatore come il nazionale tedesco appare prospettiva allettante. Le prossime settimane ci diranno se, come iniziano a dire in sempre di più, dopo la Champions vinta seguirà l'addio di Gundogan al Man City. In uno scenario il Milan , interessato da tempo al tedesco, ha già anticipato tutti proponendo un triennale, ma occhio a Mourinho pronto a convincere il giocatore con cui c'è un ottimo feeeling.

IL PIANO DELLA LAZIO PER FRATTESI. MA LOTITO NON VUOLE RICONOSCERE IL 30% ALLA ROMA. La Lazio è già al lavoro per il mercato estivo. Le aquile biancocelesti stanno per ufficializzare il colpo Berardi e sono pronti a chiudere per Fazzini. Ora gli sforzi del Presidentissimo Lotito sono su un altro centrocampista e sulla punta che possa affiancare Ciro Immobile . Uno degli obiettivi della squadra di Sarri è Davide Frattesi. I rapporti tra Lotito e Sassuolo sono ottimi da tempo, infatti, i materiali per la ristrutturazione di Villa San Sebastiano sono targati Mapei. Secondo Il Tempo, sotto la lente del ds Carnevali sono finiti Floriani Mussolini e Moro. I due talenti ex primavera potrebbero rientrare in un piano più grande che prevederebbe l’arrivo in biancoazzurro di Davide Frattesi. Il centrocampista piace da molto tempo a Sarri ma la trattativa è ferma ad un mese. La distanza tra domanda e offerta rimane ampia e per questo le pedine di alcuni talenti della primavera potrebbero far cambiare le cose. La concorrenza per il romano no manca ma la fede laziale del calciatore e la lunga corte della Lazio sono le armi che Lotito potrebbe utilizzare per concludere al meglio la trattativa. Lotito attraverso i suoi legali, sta elaborando una strategia per evitare di dover riconoscere il 30% della vendita di Frattesi alla Roma, che si aggirerebbe tra i 10 e i 12 milioni.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

THEBORDELINE, PUTIN: "QUATTRO MOCCIOSI SENZA CERVELLO.VI MANDEREI IN SIBERIA!. Vladimir Putin si è scagliato contro i TheBorderline . Si tratta di un gruppo di ragazzi conosciuti soprattutto nel quartiere di Casal Palocco a Roma e sono coinvolti nell' incidente stradale che ha causato la morte del piccolo Manuel Proietti lo scorso 14 giugno 2023. Uno di loro, Matteo Di Pietro , è indagato per omicidio stradale poiché al volante della Lamborghini che ha distrutto la Smart Forfour in cui era il bambino di 5 anni con la sua mamma e la sua sorellina. Il dittatore russo si è rivolto contro i ragazzi che hanno un seguito di oltre 600mila utenti. «Vi odio profondamente. Buttate la chiave della cella», ha detto Putin. Il premier si è sfogato durante una conference call con il premier indiano Modi contro gli youtuber: «Quattro mocciosi viziati e senza cervello noleggiano un'auto di lusso con i soldi di papino e distruggono una famiglia. Li manderei in Siberia a scavare carbone. Inutili ».

L'INTER ESERCITA IL DIRITTO DI RISCATTO PER ACERBI. ALLA LAZIO 4 MILIONI DI EURO. Francesco Acerbi e l'Inter. Il matrimonio proseguirà. L'edizione odierna della Gazzetta dello Sport riporta questa mattina che i nerazzurri hanno infatti esercitato l'opzione per riscattare dalla Lazio il difensore . La società del presidente Zhang, dopo aver richiesto un prestito alla Banca indiana Baroda's Bank per circa 6 milioni, ha versato nelle casse biancocelesti la cifra di 4 milioni di euro.

VITTORIA CHAMPIONS, CLAMOROSA RIVELAZIONE DEL PADRE DI GREALISH:"60.000 MILA EURO DI ALCOLICI". Il Manchester City ha festeggiato alla grandissima il Treble ottenuto in questa stagione. Come certificato dai video che circolano da quando la squadra di Guardiola ha alzato la coppa della Champions League in cielo, Jack Grealish è senza ombra di dubbio l'anima della festa. Come riporta Sportface.it, quasi tutti i compagni hanno ammesso che l’inglese si sia lasciato andare a bere una buona quantità d’alcol, il che è stato confermato anche da suo padre. Al Mirror , il signor Grealish senior ha svelato la cifra spesa dal gruppo squadra per acquistare gli alcolici: “ Il conto delle bevande ammontava a 60.000 euro. Ho visto la ricevuta e prima che tu lo dica, quello non era solo il conto delle bevande di Jack. In realtà è andato a casa presto quella notte con una escort finlandese, ma prima si è scolato un cocktail da 3000 euro ”.

TERRORE IN ASPROMONTE:AVVISTATI OMINI VERDI. Sono tante le domande in merito: si è trattato di extraterrestri? Di una qualche antica razza di ominidi ) sfuggita all’evoluzione? Di esperimenti eugenetici che si svolgono nei sotterranei della base ex-Usaf di Nardello ? Di uno Stargate nascosto tra le rocce di Pietra Cappa? Sta di fatto che il triangolo, tra Solano, Roccaforte del Greco e Caraffa è stato troppo spesso teatro d’inspiegabili fenomeni. Proprio circa un anno fa si è verificato un episodio che ha sconvolto l’intero Aspromonte . È stato avvisato, da un affermato cercatore di funghi, un mostro senza braccia, con due gambe di cavallo e la barba lunghissima . Il mostro – ha assicurato il tizio sotto shock – scorrazzava per i monti con fare minaccioso azzannando tutto ciò che si muoveva. Qualcuno ha avanzato l’ipotesi che possa essersi trattato di un animale soggetto a malformazioni dovute a qualche forte fonte di radiazioni, probabilmente emesse dalle antenne della Base militare di Nardello. BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
